capabilities: Apply selected CSS snippets to individual .md or .base file views via a picker in the view header
Edit, create, and save CSS snippets in a built-in editor inside Obsidian
Show or hide the snippet selector and choose its position (left or right)
Configure editor colors from presets or custom choices
disambiguation: Not a theme manager; it scopes individual CSS snippets to single file views rather than restyling the whole vault.
extras: The manifest warns the plugin has not been manually reviewed by Obsidian staff. The README requires snippets to be disabled in Settings → Appearance → CSS snippets for scoping to work, and notes complex global selectors, at-rules, or theme variables may need adjustments.
intentEvidence: apply CSS snippets to individual Markdown (.md) and Base (.base) files instead of enabling them globally
problem: Obsidian applies CSS snippets globally to the entire vault, so you cannot restyle just one note or Base file without affecting everything else.
summary: Per-file CSS snippet manager that applies chosen snippets to individual Markdown or Base file views instead of the whole vault, with a built-in snippet editor.
